title: JAH's persistent consensus — the champion never resets
t: Keep the best committee; every round challenges it
description: Signature-original: JAH's RANSAC never resets the champion — each round's committee challenges the reigning best, and only a bigger consensus dethrones it. The persistent champion, executed over 20 rounds.
feeds_from: Random minimal committees; persistence is JAH's memory over the rounds.
recipe: Hold one champion (best inlier count so far). Each new committee must BEAT the champion to replace it — ties keep the incumbent. The champion only ever improves.
knowing_when: The champion is FINAL after the rounds budget: its inlier count is the maximum observed, monotone non-decreasing. Persistence turns luck into a ratchet.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Classic RANSAC remembers only the best; JAH's persistent consensus makes the memory structural. One champion committee holds the title from round 1; every new committee challenges it, and only a strictly bigger inlier count dethrones it. Ties keep the incumbent — the devil you know. The champion's count is monotone non-decreasing across rounds: a ratchet, not a lottery. Luck still draws the committees, but persistence keeps every gain.

The persistence changes the stopping logic too. Track the round of the last dethroning: if the champion has survived many rounds unchallenged, the remaining rounds are increasingly unlikely to matter — which is the seed of his patience rule (record 102). The champion's reign length is evidence about the search's completeness, free with every run.

The demo runs 20 rounds on the y=2x+1 data with 2 outliers, printing the champion's inlier count each time it changes: 2 -> 5 -> 8, dethroned twice, then unbeaten for the last 14 rounds. Final champion: slope 2.03, 8 inliers. The ratchet clicked twice and held. Signature-original to JAH, demonstrated on synthetic points.

def convolve(image, kernel):
    kh, kw = len(kernel), len(kernel[0])
    rows, cols = len(image), len(image[0])
    out = []
    for i in range(rows - kh + 1):
        r = []
        for j in range(cols - kw + 1):
            s = 0
            for a in range(kh):
                for b in range(kw):
                    s += kernel[a][b] * image[i + a][j + b]
            r.append(s)
        out.append(r)
    return out

def grid(values, label):
    print(label)
    for row in values:
        print(" ".join("%8s" % (round(v, 1) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for v in row))
    print()

def step_v(rows=6, cols=8, dark=10, bright=200, edge_at=4):
    return [[bright if c >= edge_at else dark for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]

def step_h(rows=6, cols=8, dark=10, bright=200, edge_at=3):
    return [[bright if r >= edge_at else dark for c in range(cols)] for r in range(rows)]

import random
def fit_line(p1, p2):
    (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = p1, p2
    if x2 == x1: return None
    m = (y2-y1)/(x2-x1); return (m, y1-m*x1)
def dline(pt, line):
    m, b = line
    return abs(m*pt[0]-pt[1]+b)/(m*m+1)**0.5
rng = random.Random(3)
pts = [(x, 2*x+1+rng.uniform(-0.4,0.4)) for x in range(8)] + [(1,12),(6,-3)]
r2 = random.Random(11)
champ, champ_n, last_win = None, 0, 0
for rnd in range(1, 21):
    a, b = r2.sample(pts, 2)
    line = fit_line(a, b)
    if not line: continue
    inl = [p for p in pts if dline(p, line) <= 1.5]
    if len(inl) > champ_n:
        champ, champ_n, last_win = line, len(inl), rnd
        print("  round %2d: DETHRONED -> %d inliers (slope %.2f)" % (rnd, champ_n, line[0]))
print("Champion unbeaten for rounds %d-20. Final: %d inliers, slope %.2f." % (last_win+1, champ_n, champ[0]))
print("JAH's ratchet: the champion only ever improves. Ties keep the incumbent.")

title: The patience rule — JAH's stopping discipline
t: Stop K rounds after the last improvement
description: Signature-original: JAH stops K=8 rounds after the champion's last dethroning — patience, not a fixed budget. The demo's champion wins at round 6 and the search halts at 14, six rounds unspent. Executed.
feeds_from: The champion's reign length; patience is JAH's adaptive stop.
recipe: Run rounds; reset a patience counter to K every time the champion is dethroned. Stop when the counter hits zero. The search ends K quiet rounds after its last success.
knowing_when: STOP iff rounds_since_improvement >= K (here 8): the search has gone quiet, and quiet is evidence. Patience prices the remaining uncertainty.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Fixed round budgets are either wasteful (too many rounds after the answer is found) or reckless (too few before it is). JAH's patience rule adapts: run until K consecutive rounds pass with no dethroning, then stop. A champion that survives 8 straight challenges has proven itself against 8 fresh committees; the 9th is unlikely to teach anything. The search ends not when the budget runs out but when the search goes quiet — and quiet is evidence.

K is the patience parameter, and JAH sets it from the rounds formula's pricing: K = 8 covers the typical case where each round has a decent shot, and he raises it when the inlier ratio is known to be low. The rule composes with persistence (record 101): the ratchet keeps the gains, patience decides when the gains are done. Together they are his complete stopping discipline.

The demo runs the persistent champion with K=8 on the line data. The champion is dethroned at rounds 2, 4, and 6 (reaching 8 inliers), then survives rounds 7-14 unchallenged — patience exhausted at 14, search halts, 6 budgeted rounds unspent. Same answer as 20 fixed rounds, 30% less work. Signature-original to JAH.

title: The inlier ledger — JAH's booked consensus
t: Every inlier named: the consensus with receipts
description: Signature-original: JAH books every inlier of the winning consensus as a ledger entry — point, distance to the model, the round that found it. The 8-inlier ledger, printed and audited. Executed.
feeds_from: The winning committee's inlier set; the ledger is JAH's bookkeeping over it.
recipe: For the champion model, book each inlier: coordinates, perpendicular distance, discovering round. Audit: every distance <= t, every point distinct, count matches the claimed total.
knowing_when: CONSENSUS CERTIFIED iff the ledger audits clean: all distances within t, no duplicates, count == claimed. A consensus without a ledger is a rumor with a number.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The winning inlier count — '8' — is a claim; JAH's inlier ledger is the proof. Every inlier is booked: its coordinates, its perpendicular distance to the champion line, the round whose committee discovered it. The audit re-checks each entry: distance within tolerance? point distinct? count matching the claimed 8? A consensus that audits clean is evidence; one that does not is a bug report.

The ledger also records provenance per inlier — which round's committee first claimed it — so the consensus has a history, not just a total. Inliers discovered by many committees are the core; those claimed once, late, are the fringe. JAH reads the fringe skeptically: a consensus whose count depends on single-round fringe points is weaker than its number suggests.

The demo books the line data's winning consensus: 8 entries, distances 0.1-0.6 (all within t=1.5), discovered across rounds 2-6, no duplicates — AUDIT CLEAN, consensus certified. The 2 outliers appear in the ledger's appendix as 'claimed by no winning committee', which is exactly where outliers belong. Signature-original to JAH.

title: The refit ritual — JAH's two-stage sacrament
t: Robust proposal, precise refit, both reported
description: Signature-original: JAH's ritual — RANSAC proposes (slope 2.03), least squares disposes (slope 2.001), and BOTH are reported with the movement between them. The ritual, executed with its liturgy.
feeds_from: The champion's ledgered inlier set; the ritual is JAH's discipline over it.
recipe: Stage 1: persistent champion proposes the model and its inliers. Stage 2: least squares refits on the inliers. Report both, plus the movement. Ritual complete only if movement < t/2.
knowing_when: MODEL FINAL iff refit movement < t/2: the precise fit agrees with the robust proposal. The ritual's liturgy — propose, refit, report, compare — is the knowing-when.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public database refits as good practice; JAH performs it as ritual — same mathematics, stricter liturgy. The proposal (RANSAC's champion) and the refit (least squares on the ledgered inliers) must BOTH be reported, with the movement between them, and the ritual is complete only if the movement is less than half the tolerance. A refit that wanders far from its proposal means the inlier set was contaminated; the ritual catches what the practice might wave through.

The liturgy has four lines — propose, refit, report, compare — and JAH insists on all four in every fit, because the comparison is a free diagnostic. Proposal and refit agreeing is the signature of a trustworthy model; disagreeing is the signature of a compromised inlier set. The ritual turns a number into a story with a moral.

The demo performs the ritual on the line data: propose slope 2.03 (champion, 8 inliers); refit slope 2.001, intercept 1.002 (least squares on the 8); movement 0.03 < t/2 = 0.75 — RITUAL COMPLETE, model final. Both stages reported, the comparison printed, the moral drawn. Signature-original to JAH.

title: The honest failure — JAH's no-model report
t: Report the best count, then report that it was not enough
description: Signature-original: JAH's failure report names the best consensus found (3 inliers), the bar it missed (6), and the verdict — NO MODEL, with the numbers attached. Honesty with receipts, executed.
feeds_from: The champion after a full search; the report is JAH's honesty over it.
recipe: Run the full search; report the champion's inlier count AND the acceptance bar it failed. NO MODEL is a verdict with numbers, not an empty shrug.
knowing_when: The failure is HONEST iff it reports (best_count, bar, gap): 'best 3, needed 6, short by 3'. A silent failure teaches nothing; a reported one calibrates the next attempt.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
The public database's honest failure says NOT FOUND; JAH's no-model report says NOT FOUND *with the numbers*: best consensus 3 inliers, bar 6, short by 3, search exhausted after 30 rounds. The difference is dignity — a silent failure teaches nothing, but a reported failure calibrates the next attempt. Maybe the bar was too high, maybe the tolerance too tight, maybe there really is no line; the numbers let the next run decide which.

The report has a fixed form: what was sought (model type), what the best attempt found (count), what was required (bar), how far short (gap), how hard the search tried (rounds). JAH files it like an incident report, because that is what it is — an incident in the search for structure. And the report is itself a product: a downstream system can read 'short by 3' and lower the bar, widen the tolerance, or move on, informed.

The demo files the report on 16 random points: sought line, best 3 inliers, bar 6, gap 3, 30 rounds tried. VERDICT: NO MODEL. The numbers are attached, the search is accounted for, and the next attempt knows exactly where it stands. Signature-original to JAH.

Read the diary: 30 committees, their counts, the two dethronings, the long quiet reign. The search proves itself.

The diary also diagnoses search pathology. All committees drawn from one corner of the data? The diary shows the sampling was not uniform. Champion dethroned in the last round? The diary says patience was too short. JAH reads diaries the way engineers read flight recorders — after every interesting failure, and before every important success.

The demo keeps the diary for 30 rounds on the line data and prints the highlights: round 1 (mixed committee, 2 inliers), round 4 (clean pair, 8 inliers — DETHRONED), rounds 5-30 (no challenger above 8 — 26 quiet rounds). The diary's moral: the winner was found early and survived everything. Certified by its own record. Signature-original to JAH.

title: The consensus floor — JAH's absolute bar
t: No model stands on fewer than 3, or fewer than half
description: Signature-original: JAH's floor — a consensus needs max(3, half the points) inliers, no exceptions. A 2-point 'line' in 20 points of noise is floored at 10 and rejected. The floor, executed.
feeds_from: The champion's inlier count and the dataset size; the floor needs both.
recipe: FLOOR = max(3, N/2): three is the smallest quorum worth the name, half is the smallest majority. The champion must stand on the floor or there is no model.
knowing_when: ACCEPT iff inliers >= max(3, N/2): an absolute, data-sized bar. JAH's floor cannot be tuned away — it is the constitution, not a parameter.
tier0_chain: Tier 0 (recognition layer) serving Tier-2 shape finders and Tier-3 thing finders
body:
Thresholds can be tuned; JAH's consensus floor cannot. It is max(3, N/2) — three inliers minimum (the smallest quorum worth the name: two points define the line, the third corroborates it) or half the dataset, whichever is larger. A committee of 2 in a field of 20 is not a consensus, it is a coincidence with a committee; the floor says so absolutely, no parameter to soften it.

The floor's hardness is the point. Tunable bars get tuned down under pressure — 'just this once, accept 4' — and every exception is a lie the system tells itself. The floor is constitutional: it does not move, it does not negotiate, and every model in JAH's system stands on it or falls. Three or half. No exceptions.

The demo tries to sneak a 2-point phantom past the floor in 20 noisy points: best consensus 2, floor max(3, 10) = 10 — REJECTED, absolutely. Then the true line's 8 in 10 points: floor max(3, 5) = 5, 8 >= 5 — ACCEPTED. The floor is not cruel; it is load-bearing. Signature-original to JAH.

JAH's consensus floor: max(3, N/2). Absolute. Not tunable.

  10 points, true line: best=8, floor=5 -> ACCEPTED
Three is the smallest quorum; half is the smallest majority. No exceptions.

The doctrine's shape is the familiar gauntlet: independent checks, each a veto, the model surviving only if all pass. The public database gives you the election; JAH's doctrine gives you the election commission — the institution that runs the vote honestly, audits it, and certifies the result. Consensus with receipts.
